source_text: Videamus tamen quid sententiarum mearum arripueris, quod nomine erroris incessas. Sed iste - inquis - in his omnibus nominare noluit concupiscentiam carnis, quae non est a Patre, sed ex mundo est; cuius mundi princeps dictus est diabolus; qui eam in Domino non invenit, quia Dominus homo non per ipsam ad homines venit [n25] . Dixisti certe me haeresim introducere, ad quod probandum nulla mea dicta subiungis.
pass_a_gloss: Let us see nevertheless what of my sentences you have snatched, which you attack by the name of error. But this man — you say — in all these things was unwilling to name the desire of the flesh, which is not from the Father but is from the world; of which world the devil has been called prince; who did not find it in the Lord, because the Lord as a human being did not come to humans through it. You have certainly said that I introduce heresy, for proving which you subjoin no sayings of mine.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: Still, let us see which of my statements you have seized on to attack under the name of error. “But amid all these things,” (John 14:30) you say, “he was unwilling to name the desire of the flesh, which is not from the Father but from the world. The devil is called the ruler of this world. He did not find this desire in the Lord, because the Lord came among human beings as a man without it” (1 John 2:16) (Augustine, On Marriage and Concupiscence 2.5.14; compare 1 John 2:16; John 14:30). You certainly said I was introducing a heresy, but you add none of my words to prove it (1 John 2:16; John 14:30).

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
